title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
oneLinerQuestion: Find the median of two sorted arrays in logarithmic time complexity.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: To find the median of two sorted arrays of lengths m and n in optimal O(log(min(m, n))) time, we must avoid merging the arrays (which takes O(m + n)). Instead, we frame the problem as finding a cut or partition that splits the combined elements into two halves (Left and Right) of equal size, such that every element in the combined Left half is less than or equal to every element in the combined Right half.

- Step 1: Enforce Search on Smaller Array — We ensure binary search runs on the smaller array (if nums1.length > nums2.length, swap them). This guarantees that the binary search completes in O(log(min(m, n))) time and ensures the partition index in the larger array is always valid and non-negative.

- Step 2: Establish the Partition Invariant — We set binary search boundaries 'low = 0' and 'high = m'. For any partition cut 'i' in nums1 (midpoint of low and high), the corresponding cut 'j' in nums2 is fixed by the formula: j = Math.floor((m + n + 1) / 2) - i. This maintains that the total count of elements on the left half equals the total count on the right half (or has exactly one extra element on the left if total length is odd).

- Step 3: Identify Boundary Elements — We identify the four boundary values surrounding the cuts: maxLeft1 = (i === 0) ? -Infinity : nums1[i - 1], minRight1 = (i === m) ? Infinity : nums1[i], maxLeft2 = (j === 0) ? -Infinity : nums2[j - 1], and minRight2 = (j === n) ? Infinity : nums2[j]. Using -Infinity and Infinity cleanly resolves array edge boundaries without special conditional checks.

- Step 4: Validate Partition & Adjust Search Range — A partition is valid if both (maxLeft1 <= minRight2) and (maxLeft2 <= minRight1) hold true. If maxLeft1 > minRight2, the cut in nums1 is too far right, so we shift 'high = i - 1'. If maxLeft2 > minRight1, the cut in nums1 is too far left, so we shift 'low = i + 1'.

- Step 5: Median Extraction — Once a valid partition is found, if the combined length (m + n) is odd, the median is the largest element on the left side: Math.max(maxLeft1, maxLeft2). If the combined length is even, the median is the average of the two middle elements: (Math.max(maxLeft1, maxLeft2) + Math.min(minRight1, minRight2)) / 2.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(log(min(m, n))) since binary search is performed strictly over the length of the smaller array. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space as we only maintain boundary pointers and primitive partition variables.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION findMedianSortedArrays(nums1, nums2):
    IF LENGTH(nums1) > LENGTH(nums2) THEN RETURN findMedianSortedArrays(nums2, nums1)
    m = LENGTH(nums1), n = LENGTH(nums2), low = 0, high = m
    WHILE low <= high DO:
        i = (low + high) / 2, j = (m + n + 1) / 2 - i
        maxLeft1 = (i == 0) ? -INF : nums1[i-1]
        minRight1 = (i == m) ? INF : nums1[i]
        maxLeft2 = (j == 0) ? -INF : nums2[j-1]
        minRight2 = (j == n) ? INF : nums2[j]
        IF maxLeft1 <= minRight2 AND maxLeft2 <= minRight1 THEN:
            IF (m + n) % 2 == 0 THEN RETURN (MAX(maxLeft1, maxLeft2) + MIN(minRight1, minRight2)) / 2.0
            ELSE RETURN MAX(maxLeft1, maxLeft2)
        ELSE IF maxLeft1 > minRight2 THEN high = i - 1
        ELSE low = i + 1
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION
